- When sentiment turns negative sharply (especially >0.67 → <0.33 or drop >0.67), reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment remains positive for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sentiment spike (e.g., >0.67 for 2+ days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.  
- If news volume drops below 2.0 for 2+ days, reduce forecast by 3–7% to reflect reduced market momentum.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply 3–5% downward adjustment for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment change is negative and cumulative (e.g., -0.33 over 3+ days), forecast should trend downward; apply linear decay adjustment.  
- When sentiment is flat (±0.33 for 3+ days), model tends to drift; use 2–4% mean-reversion correction toward recent 7-day average.
